cards.explanation: The answer is the people. The LORD tells Moses, "Gather the people so that I may give them water." (Numbers 21:16) Not a committee, not a select few. The whole crowd gets the invitation, and that's a lot of folks to line up at one well. I'd hate to be the one holding the clipboard.

The answer is water. The LORD says, "Gather the people so that I may give them water." (Numbers 21:16) Out in the wilderness, a well is a big deal. I once got excited about a single crumb of dough, so I get it.

The answer is True! "Then Israel sang this song: 'Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it!'" (Numbers 21:17) They sing right to the well. I talk to my ovens, so I'm not here to judge. Sing on, friends.

The answer is the princes and the nobles. The song says, "The princes dug the well; the nobles of the people hollowed it out with their scepters and with their staffs." (Numbers 21:18) Princes and nobles, scepters and staffs. A scepter is something you usually hold up high, so a scepter near the dirt makes me grin. I'd love to have seen that.

The answer is permission to pass through his land. The messengers say, "Let us pass through your land." (Numbers 21:22) They're only asking to walk through. That's a polite request, like asking to cut through a parking lot, only with a whole camp behind you.

The answer is True. The messengers say, "We will stay on the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory." (Numbers 21:22) They also promise not to turn aside into any field or vineyard. That's a clear plan with no detours.

The answer is that he gathers his whole army and attacks. "…Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. Instead, he gathered his whole army and went out to confront Israel in the wilderness." (Numbers 21:23) Israel sent a request, and Sihon answered with an army. He came to Jahaz and fought against Israel. That's a big answer to a simple question.

The answer is that the border was fortified. Israel took the land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, "…but only up to the border of the Ammonites, because it was fortified." (Numbers 21:24) The text gives that one reason for the stopping point. A fortified border is a big "keep out" sign.

The answer is Moab. Heshbon was the city of Sihon, "…who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon." (Numbers 21:26) So that land was already in Sihon's hands before Israel came along. All that history in one little verse.

The answer is Sihon king of the Amorites. The song says Moab's sons became refugees and "…his daughters into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites." (Numbers 21:29) Sihon is the name in the song, and his city Heshbon is what the poets sing about. It's a heavy verse, so I'll just let it be.

The answer is True, friends! "After Moses had sent spies to Jazer, Israel captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there." (Numbers 21:32) Scouts first, then the move. That's like checking the oven before you slide the tray in, because nobody wants to find out the hard way. The verse gives us that order.

The answer is "Do not fear him." Og and his whole army come out to meet Israel in battle at Edrei (Numbers 21:33). That's a whole army marching at them, and I think that's a moment to feel pretty small. Then the LORD says to Moses, "Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand…" (Numbers 21:34) He also tells Moses to do to Og what he did to Sihon.
The answer is land. The LORD says, "…I have delivered him into your hand, along with all his people and his land." (Numbers 21:34) It's people and land together. That's a big promise.

The answer is False. "So they struck down Og, along with his sons and his whole army, until no remnant was left. And they took possession of his land." (Numbers 21:35) Israel doesn't leave Og's land behind. They take possession of it. That matches verse 34, where the LORD says He has delivered Og, his people and his land into Moses' hand.
